journey.name: TL-21 Two taps on a checkbox during one write both mean complete
journey.description:
KNOWN-DEFECT WATCHLIST. Asserts the current behaviour; whether it is the right behaviour is a product call. See qa/TEST-PLAN.md.
The checkbox renders task.isCompleted, which is the cache, which does not change until the write returns. So a second tap during the first write computes its value from the same stale false and sends "complete" again: two taps that a user reads as complete-then-undo leave the task complete, with no error and nothing to say a tap was absorbed.
Neither tap is optimistic and neither is rejected - the control is live throughout the call, and DefaultTaskRepository.setCompleted re-reads the current fields from the cache, so the second write carries the same flag as the first.
Invisible to a unit test: a test dispatcher lets the first call complete before the second tap is dispatched, which is exactly the interleaving that does not happen on a device. Pinning the latency at 3000 ms makes the real one reachable by hand.
Preconditions: adb shell am force-stop com.rounds.test.to_dolist adb shell am start -n com.rounds.test.to_dolist/.MainActivity --es qa_failure_rate 0.0 --es qa_latency_ms 3000

actions.action: Verify that the "Renew domain registration" row has an unchecked checkbox
Tap the checkbox with the content description "Mark complete" on the "Renew domain registration" row
Immediately tap that same checkbox a second time, within half a second, while the first write is still in flight
Wait ten seconds for both writes to finish
Verify that the "Renew domain registration" row has a checked checkbox
Verify that the "Renew domain registration" title is struck through
Verify that no error message is on screen
Verify that the checkbox on that row is now described as "Mark incomplete"
